decision.title: The Swift full surface: XQuery, XSLT, XSD and the DUCET resource (packet )
decision.summary: The Swift module Sxml gains XQuery, XSLT and XSD over the host shim's full-module entry points, and CollationData.bundled serves a copied DUCET as a SwiftPM resource.

body.p: , after , , , . Packet added the rest of the task file's Swift API to module Sxml, over the host shim's full-module entry points. No C changed.

item.p: compileQuery(_:namespaces:baseURI:) gives an XQuery with evaluate(context:variables:updates:messages:), serialize(_:), run(...) and isUpdating.
UpdateSink is a struct of two optional throwing closures, updatedTree and putDocument. PutDocument.serialize() uses method xml without parameters, as in JavaScript.

compileStylesheet(_:baseURI:staticParameters:) (a String, or [UInt8]) gives a Stylesheet. transform(...) takes JavaScript's options as labels; args is arguments:. It returns a TransformResult (output, value, resultDocuments).
InitialMode is .named(String) or .unnamed, and a string literal names a mode. It replaces JavaScript's '#unnamed', as Kotlin's InitialMode.Unnamed does.

ResultDelivery, ValidationMode and Validity are enums. Their raw values are those of sxml_xslt_result_delivery and sxml_validation_mode (sxml_host.h does not include xslt.h or schema.h) and, for Validity, the JavaScript names.

compileSchema(_:baseURI:) takes a String, one SchemaDocument or an array of them (.text(_:uri:), .bytes(_:uri:), .resolved(_:)). Schema.validate(_:mode:type:uri:) takes a String, [UInt8] or a Value (a node takes no uri:).
SchemaError is a struct (error: SxmlError, reports), as the task file says, not a subtype of SxmlError. So a caller that catches SxmlError does not catch a schema that fails to compile.
The messages closure and the sink's closures run after the call, with the failure read first, so they may use the processor (). An error a closure throws replaces the call's own failure.
DUCET: CollationData.bundled serves bindings/swift/Sources/Sxml/Resources/allkeys.txt, a .copy resource read through Bundle.module once per process, when a UCA collation first asks for it.

Deviation: the resource is a copy of third_party/unicode-collation/allkeys.txt, not a symbolic link. SwiftPM copies a link into the bundle as a link, which then dangles. The copy has the same git blob, so the repository does not grow. A test checks that the two files are equal. Whoever updates the DUCET updates both.
Tests: FullTests.swift has 28 Swift Testing tests.
24 have the names, inputs and expected text of full.test.ts: 10 XQuery, 8 XSLT, 5 XSD, and the full allocation-failure loop.

Two tests of full.test.ts have no counterpart. The core-module refusal does not apply, because the native library has every language. The disposal test is replaced by "queries, stylesheets and schemas keep their processor alive" (ARC).
3 resource data tests: the bundled DUCET, timezone-data served from third_party/tzdata/zoneinfo, and locale-data served from third_party/cldr/common.
ctest swift/linux (debug preset, ASan): 55 tests pass with 0 leaks (was 27), both allocation-failure loops included. The run takes 69 s.
Task file: its Swift example ends with result.serialize(["method": "json"]) on a two-item result, which raises SERE0023. The READMEs use other examples.

For 6.9 (Apple): the resource needs nothing more. Bundle.module finds it in the package's bundle on Apple platforms too. Check CollationData.bundled there with the test "the bundled DUCET is the vendored one, and UCA collations use it". A package that depends on Sxml links the XCFramework, and the resource still comes from the Sxml target.
